text:
mae: seen a new intake from vulnfeed — CVE-2026-FASTJSON-01, fastjson < 2.5.4 memory corruption leading to RCE. EPSS high, PoC reported on GH.

diego: link? :eyes:

mae: https://example.com/CVE-2026-FASTJSON-01 (paste of vulnfeed). EPSS 0.78, CVSS 9.1 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H). PoC gist included.

cve-bot: automated triage: package=fastjson, affected_versions=<2.5.4, exploitability=remote, known_poc=yes, recommended_action=patch ASAP

lena: quick ask — where does fastjson live in our stack? I recall one usage in legacy ingestion microservices and in a small python lambda wrapper for telemetry parsing.

ash: confirmed: services: ingest-parser, legacy-proxy; also present in a vendor dependency inside metric-exporter (jar). No direct exposure from public endpoints for metric-exporter, ingest-parser parses untrusted JSON from customers.

ryan: that's bad. ingest-parser handles customer payloads — risk: direct attacker-supplied JSON. Prioritize.

mae: tentative severity = P0 for ingest-parser, P1 for vendor metric-exporter. Need owners, quick mitigation plan: patch, backport, temporary WAF rule or drop specific object shapes?

diego: owners: @ingest-team -> ash, @platform-java -> ryan (metric-exporter). I'll create two tickets and assign. Can we hotpatch ingest-parser today?

ash: can deploy a patch to ingest-parser if we have a PR and CI green. But deploy perms need RBAC temporarily widened for hotpatch on prod due to release freeze. @mae can you sign off for emergency exception?

mae: yes, emergency RBAC exception approved for the ingest-team only. Please follow emergency release playbook and add audit log entries. Tag me on PR.

lena: for metric-exporter (java) we should coordinate with platform-java; may need a shaded dependency bump and rebuild. ETA 24-48h.

ryan: agree. I'll start a minimal backport branch to 2.5.4 and run smoke tests. If PoC triggers local exploit, we'll validate patch efficacy.

mae: mitigation options documented: 1) patch to 2.5.4+ 2) WAF rule to block Content-Type/JSON bodies > certain nested depth (temp) 3) instrument runtime to drop suspicious constructs. Preferred = patch + RBACed hotfix for ingest-parser.

ash: WAF rule could be quick, but false positives risk for customers. Prefer patch.

cve-bot: recommended CI checks: add exploit regression test, run fuzzing harness in canary for next 12h.

diego: small checklist I'm adding to ticket: 1) confirm vulnerable coordinates in SBOM 2) run PoC against staging 3) patch PR + security review 4) emergency RBAC exception + deploy 5) post-deploy canary + fuzz 6) close with audit log links.

mae: SBOM note — inventory shows fastjson v2.4.9 in ingest-parser jar. Metric-exporter uses v2.3.0 (shaded). We'll need two PRs.

ryan: working on PoC in local, seeing crash w/ nested map arrays. POC snippet:

```
{"@type":"fastjson.Class","val":"..."}
```

mae: good. If PoC reproduces, escalate to Incident channel and follow incident runbook.

ash: can we temporarily block customer JSON uploads for ingest-parser customers with suspicious activity? Ops can throttle per-tenant.

diego: ops, can you add per-tenant throttle/ingest quarantine for the next 24h for high-risk tenants? @ops-team

deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy for ingest-parser-urgent-fix at 2026-03-20T15:30Z (pending PR merge and RBAC approval)

mae: I will post final decision in 30m after quick risk call. For now: P0 for ingest-parser, P1 for metric-exporter. Owners assigned. Action: patch + canary + fuzzing.

lena: adding note: KMS/keys unaffected. This is pure deserialization vuln. Audit logging required for the emergency RBAC change (who granted, when).

ryan: I'll attach PoC output and CI test to the PR. ETA for ingest-parser PR: 2h.

mae: thanks — keep thread updated. If PoC escalates, we'll create incident and bring oncall.

cve-bot: note: CVE record updated with exploit tag. Subscribe for updates: #security-notifs

mae: closing temporary triage — follow tickets for steps. :white_check_mark:
